title: Reward Hacking Detection as a Precursor to Monitor Evasion

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If action monitors cannot catch reward hacking early, the control chain has a structural blind spot. Connecting reward hacking to monitor evasion bridges RL safety and control monitoring literatures in a valuable way.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing an RL fine-tuning experiment with proxy reward optimization, building both action-level and outcome-level monitors, and measuring detection lag. This is an advanced ML research project requiring substantial RL expertise far beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: RL fine-tuning, monitor implementation, and detection-lag measurement are three substantial tasks. RL experiments alone are notoriously time-consuming and unpredictable. Far exceeds 30-hour budget.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
